Every picture from any decoder is checked against its declared format (plane count and exact plane bytes) before it can reach the sink; a mismatch is DecoderFault::Protocol. Never fires for rav1d (the in-process path builds planes from the format), it exists for external decoders.

ReelError gained a variant (not non_exhaustive): exhaustive matches would break; inside reel only code() and outcome_for matched exhaustively (both updated); the only dependent crate (reel-native) uses wildcard arms and compiled unchanged.

INTEGRATE (removes ~250 duplicated lines in src/host.rs: Plan/Demux/Pump/Forward/verify_grant/read_head/check_cancel): implement hsk_studio_reel::ExternalVideoDecoder for WorkerAv1Provider. identity() = DecoderIdentity{id: av1::DECODER_ID, version: av1::decoder_version()} (HELLO already verifies it); supports(VideoCodec::Av1); open(spec, cancel) = parse_av1c(spec.config) if non-empty, frame_cap = declared_frame_cap(cfg, spec.width, spec.height, &spec.limits), checkout worker, OPEN{max_chunk_bytes: decoder_budget(spec.width, spec.height, &spec.limits), color: spec.color, config: spec.config}, return a session owning the lease + Clock; VideoDecodeSession::send = PACKET exchange whose on_frame converts WireFrame -> DecodedPicture and calls out.accept; finish = FINISH exchange. Then wire the host with Registry::standard().with_video_decoder(Arc::new(worker.clone())): untrusted isobmff/matroska Decoded requests reach the worker through the normal registry calls and reel's pump does matching, pre-roll, format-change and receipt fields. decode_av1 / the av1 provider id can stay as a thin wrapper or be retired.

FAULTS: in the session return VideoDecodeError::Fault(DecoderFault::Crashed | Deadline | Protocol) for Av1WorkerFault::DecoderCrashed | DecoderDeadline | Protocol and update Av1Error::into_reel to ReelError::DecoderFault{fault} for those three; keep OutputTooLarge, RespawnLimited, PoolBusy -> LimitExceeded, VersionMismatch -> Unsupported, SpawnFailed -> CodecUnavailable. DecoderFault::code() strings equal the existing reel-native codes (decoder_crashed, decoder_deadline), worker_protocol becomes decoder_protocol.

CANCEL/DEADLINE: the route passes the caller's CancellationToken to open, send and finish; reel-native's Clock{cancel, segment_wall} maps to it unchanged. VideoStreamSpec.limits carries Limits (max_chunk_bytes for caps), width/height are the container-declared size (0 = undeclared, then fall back to limits).

NO-LINK SPLIT (feature requirement 3): routing and the AV1 record parser/descriptor need no reel feature any more (Av1Config, parse_av1c, av1_descriptor at the crate root). A host image without rav1d still needs the worker binary (which uses av1::Av1Decoder, feature av1) in a SEPARATE package, because Cargo unifies features per package: new worker package (root Cargo.toml edit = steward) depending on reel with features=["av1"], host package depending on reel WITHOUT av1. DecoderIdentity takes &'static str, so a host without rav1d needs a build-time constant (or interning) for the worker's decoder version instead of av1::decoder_version().

DEFAULTS for embedders: untrusted media -> Registry with_video_decoder(worker) and plain decode_segment; do not pass SourceTrust::Trusted for imports. Trusted is for generated fixtures and content the caller has hashed against a known-good digest.

slice4_mxf.authority: SMPTE ST 377-1:2019 (https://pub.smpte.org/pub/st377-1/st377-1-2019.pdf, readable; sections 6.3 KLV, 6.4.1 KAG, 6.6 run-in, 7 partitions, 9.1-9.3 header metadata + Primer, 9.6.1 set keys, 11 index tables, Annex A/B/E/F/H). ST 378 (OP1a), ST 390 (OP-Atom), ST 379 (Generic Container) and ST 400 (labels) were NOT read: UNVERIFIED are the operational pattern labels (reader reports the label, accepts any pattern), the Generic Container keys used to find essence elements (06.0e.2b.34.01.02.01.vv.0d.01.03.01 + track number; system items 0d.01.03.01.04.xx) and the ST 400 data definition labels used by classify(); all three were checked only against ffmpeg-written files and libavformat positions.
slice4_mxf.oracles: ffprobe -show_packets (pos/pts/dts/size/flags) of two ffmpeg 8.1.1 files; independent Python parse (klvdump/metadump written from the spec) agrees with the Rust index entries for the OP1a file; synthetic file built in the test from ST 377-1 layouts for the multi-partition constant-size path.
decisions: Partitions: footer chain validated (this_partition agreement, strictly decreasing links, first pack must be a footer, last must be the header) else KLV scan; RIP not used.

Essence start = first byte after pack, optional Fill, HeaderByteCount, IndexByteCount and any Fill (spec 6.2.1 item order: leading Fill is not essence); stream offset -> file offset via the last partition of the BodySID with body_offset <= offset.
Header metadata from the LAST complete (status 3/4) partition carrying metadata, else the first carrying any.
Property ULs matched by their last 8 bytes (registry version byte ignored) through the Primer; index segments use static tags (spec: Primer is not used for index tables).

Temporal reordering applies only to picture tracks of variable-size indexes (11.1.6); random access = flags bit 7 (open GOP I pictures have it clear in ffmpeg files, so pre-roll walks back to the previous RA entry); sync on chunks = RA bit for pictures, true otherwise.

Wrapping heuristic: OP-Atom label byte 13 == 0x10 with a constant-size index, or a Generic Container essence label with wrapping byte 2, is clip wrapped (stream offsets exclude the KL); else frame wrapped. ffmpeg's OP-Atom file labels BWF as frame wrapped (byte 1) although it is clip wrapped, so the OP-Atom rule is needed. A wrong guess surfaces as Corrupt mxf-index-points-outside-essence / mxf-stream-offset-outside-essence, never a fabricated offset.
not_proven: NOT_PROVEN: index repetition across body partitions with different segments (only identical header/footer copies are collapsed; overlapping non-identical segments are refused as Corrupt mxf-index-overlap but that refusal is untested on a real file).
NOT_PROVEN: RIP, sparse/partial index tables, clip-wrapped essence over several partitions, DM/ST 410 generic stream partitions, run-in > 0 (code path exists in find_header_partition; no fixture).
NOT_PROVEN: any MXF essence decode (opaque by design); AES3/Wave/MPEG descriptors beyond the properties listed in meta.rs.
